pointers.sentence: Before any middleware runs, the handler does the same four things for every request, in this order: it keeps the script prefix, sends the `request_started` signal, makes the request object, and calls `BaseHandler.get_response`, which sets the URLconf and calls the chain (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIHandler.__call__`, `django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.get_response`).

Before any middleware runs, the handler does the same four things for every request, in this order: it keeps the script prefix, sends the `request_started` signal, makes the request object, and calls `BaseHandler.get_response`, which sets the URLconf and calls the chain (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIHandler.__call__`, `django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.get_response`).

The script prefix and the URLconf are both kept for the current thread: the URLconf is `settings.ROOT_URLCONF`, and the prefix is the part of the path the server mounted Django under, with a slash at its end, here `"/"` alone, since this request's environ gives no script name, the empty one becomes the prefix, and `set_script_prefix` puts the slash on its end; every URL that `reverse` builds begins with it (`django/urls/base.py:set_script_prefix`, `django/urls/base.py:set_urlconf`).

A signal is a list of receivers, and sending it calls the synchronous receivers in turn and then any asynchronous ones concurrently (`django/dispatch/dispatcher.py:Signal.send`).

The two receivers of `request_started` belong to the database layer: `reset_queries` empties the query logs of the thread's connections; `close_old_connections` closes those past their configured age or unusable after an error (`django/db/__init__.py:close_old_connections`).

[Making the request: `WSGIRequest` and `ASGIRequest`](../http/request.md) tells what the constructor sets, and [The body: `body`, `POST` and `FILES`](../http/body.md) what may be read after what (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest.__init__`, `django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest.COOKIES`).

Each is built on `MiddlewareMixin`, so each layer's call is `MiddlewareMixin.__call__`: it runs the class's `process_request` if it has one, calls the layer inside unless that returned a response, and runs the class's `process_response`, if any, on what comes back (`django/middleware/__init__.py:MiddlewareMixin.__call__`).

Another hook, `process_view`, is run not by the layer but by the handler, at the centre, once the view is known ([The URL is resolved and the view is called](view.md)) (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`).

**`SecurityMiddleware`** would answer this request, which is not secure, with a permanent redirect to HTTPS if `settings.SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT` were true, which by default it is not; its work is on the way out (`django/middleware/security.py:SecurityMiddleware.process_request`).
It sets `HttpRequest.session` to a new session store for that key (`django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py:SessionMiddleware.process_request`).

The store does not touch the database: it keeps the key, and the session's data is loaded the first time anything reads it (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.__init__`, `django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase._get_session`).

A host that is not allowed raises `DisallowedHost`, a `SuspiciousOperation`, which the `convert_exception_to_response` wrapper around this layer turns into a 400 response (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).
When `settings.PREPEND_WWW` is set, it redirects a host without `"www."` (`django/middleware/common.py:CommonMiddleware.process_request`, `django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.get_host`).

**`CsrfViewMiddleware`** reads the CSRF cookie, if the request carries one, and puts the secret a well-formed cookie holds into `HttpRequest.META` under `"CSRF_COOKIE"` for the rest of the request to use (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware.process_request`, `django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware._get_secret`).

It sets `HttpRequest.user` to a `SimpleLazyObject` around a function that will find the user, and `HttpRequest.auser` to its asynchronous twin (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:AuthenticationMiddleware.process_request`).

Nothing is looked up until the lazy object is first used: then `django.contrib.auth.get_user` takes the user's id and backend from the session and asks that backend for the user, which is a query (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:get_user`).

The default is `FallbackStorage`, which keeps messages in a cookie and falls back to the session for what does not fit, as [Message storage: `CookieStorage`, `SessionStorage` and `FallbackStorage`](../auth/message-storage.md) tells (`django/contrib/messages/middleware.py:MessageMiddleware.process_request`, `django/contrib/messages/storage/fallback.py:FallbackStorage`).
